answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can use staked identity with quadratic voice: each agent locks a bond before it can vote or post, and voting power grows only with the square root of that stake. A fake swarm of sparrow clients is therefore never cheap, since every new alias needs its own bond, and splitting one wallet into many buys no extra influence. Identities with a hollow record or no attestations stay capped until they earn trust over time. If an agent is caught double-voting, its copper bond is slashed, so a sustained attack costs far more than any benefit it could reap.
